title: stabilize-sse-heartbeat-fence-and-delimiter-normalizer-to-rescue-partial-json
author: Nina Patel
description:
Summary: This PR hardens the OpenAI-compat SSE path against a class of partial-JSON and delimiter-splitting regressions observed in tail-drop and retransmit scenarios.
The change introduces two cooperating mechanisms: 1) a lightweight heartbeat-fence marker that preserves event epoch boundaries under bursty backpressure and 2) a delimiter-normalizer that canonicalizes and emits a stable delimiter table for multi-byte/escaped sequences so downstream parsers can resynchronize without losing function-call or structured-output boundaries.

Motivation: We saw multiple incidents where streaming consumers reconstructed broken JSON objects because an escaped quote or multi-byte UTF-8 sequence was split across fragments and combined with delayed heartbeats, causing downstream reconstructor heuristics to misinterpret the sequence as an event boundary. This surfaced most often with function-call tokens and nested JSON outputs.

Design:
- Heartbeat fence: emit an idempotent fence event (":fence:epoch=<N>\n") when the runtime detects a sequence of N small fragments or after a retransmit/replay window. Consumers treat it as a non-JSON sentinel that indicates the boundary between two reliable reassembly epochs. The fence is optional for OpenAI-compat only and is ignored when the connection is native Redwood binary.
- Delimiter normalizer: when a fragment boundary splits an escape or multibyte sequence, the normalizer rewrites the emitted bytes into a canonical, resumable form and appends a small checksum tag for the tail of the fragment. This improves detector confidence when performing mid-stream resync.
- Backoff integration: fences are rate-limited and can be disabled per-client via a header to avoid adding latency when not needed.
- Tool-call handoff: ensure function-call sentinel ordering is preserved by flushing the current fence before emitting a tool-call sentinel so the consumer can deterministically apply the tool invocation.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement heartbeat-fence emitter in sse_emitter.go
- [x] Add delimiter-normalizer in stream_sanitizer.go
- [x] Update OpenAI-compat parser to skip fence events and use checksum hints
- [x] Add telemetry for fence emission rate and checksum mismatch rates
- [x] Add unit tests for split-UTF8 and split-escape cases
- [x] Add integration test that simulates retransmit + burst and validates JSON reassembly
- [x] Documentation note in docs/openai_streaming.md

Changes (high level):
- sse/emitter/sse_emitter.go: add fence emission logic and a small in-memory epoch counter
- sse/sanitizer/stream_sanitizer.go: new delimiter normalizer and checksum hint generator
- openai_compat/parser.go: add fence-skip and checksum hint consumer path
- api/tests/streaming_reassembly_test.go: new integration scenarios
- docs/openai_streaming.md: document the fence and header to disable
- telemetry/metrics_defs.yaml: new metrics: sse.fence.emitted, sse.delim_checksum_mismatch

Commits (summary):
- 7f2b3a2: initial heartbeat-fence emitter and tests
- 9d4e8f0: delimiter-normalizer implementation + unit tests for UTF-8 split cases
- b1c4d11: wire fence into OpenAI-compat parser and add checksum hints
- c4a7a90: add integration test with retransmit simulation and CI harness
- d2f8aa7: docs and telemetry + small refactor requested by reviewers

Tests & CI:
- Local unit test suite: passed (new sanitizer and emitter unit tests included)
- Integration test: added a simulated packet-drop harness; initially flaky on CI; fixed by increasing fence debounce window
- CI checks: linux-unit (pass), macos-unit (pass), go-lint (pass), npm-docs-site-build (pass), integration-replay (flaky->rerun->pass)
- Final CI status: pass

Review Conversation (high level single-string transcript): "Reviewer: Marco Ruiz — the sanitizer looks good but can we avoid emitting fences for every tiny client? Nina: added debounce and an opt-out header (x-rw-sse-fence: disabled). Reviewer: Aisha Khan — checksum approach is clever, please document expected false-positive rate; Nina: added telemetry and a doc note with numbers from test harness (false-positive < 0.02% at 64-byte window). Reviewer: Daniel Lee — ensure this doesn't change ordering semantics for function calls; Nina: altered emitter to flush fence before tool-call sentinel and added integration test to verify ordering. Reviewer: Marco Ruiz — nit: rename epoch->fence_epoch for clarity; Nina: updated variable names. Approvals: Marco Ruiz (LGTM), Aisha Khan (LGTM), Daniel Lee (LGTM). Merge strategy: squash and merge."
Release_notes: Stabilize OpenAI-compat SSE streaming by adding heartbeat fence and delimiter normalization; reduces partial-JSON reassembly errors under bursty retransmit scenarios. Opt-out header available for clients concerned with minimal emitter overhead.
